Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > Blood Magic
Chunk.text:
Blood Magic
If you are doing a no-rocket run, this mod is one of the only avenues to progress into EV, as summoning meteors is how you will obtain resources such as Titanium. Doing so may increase your warp effects.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
Chunk.text:
Progression
Progression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:
• Gallium -
There is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.
• Arsenic -
Cobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.
• Aluminum -
Aluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the "raw Aluminum" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV
Chunk.text:
End Of HV
After collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.
Spending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!
Infrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!

Chunk.title: Extreme Voltage (EV)
section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Your second rocket / Late-EV
Chunk.text:
Your second rocket / Late-EV
After getting the EV field generator you needed for the rocket computer, it's time to build your second rocket. It's a pretty straightforward step. If you forgot or didn't get much meteoric iron, you have to get back to the moon and mine some. I recommend you to have 12 stacks or 45 stacks if you don't want to go back to the moon again for meteoric iron (also for t3 rocket). With the exception of several new parts, which are booster and t2 landing module, the rest goes the same as t1 rocket but is more expensive.
You only need a trip to mars for you to get all the resources needed. Also, T2 lander doesn't need you to slow down when approaching as it's a balloon that bounces after it reaches the surface. Your mission there is to collect desh vein (it also has tungsten ore), tungsten vein (also provides lithium), and pitchblende vein (also provides thorium) if you didn't get enough uranium by centrifuging thorium ore. Remember to explore mars more for finding the mars dungeon which contains the T3 rocket blueprint.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Crafting Tier 2+ Rockets
Entrance to a Moon Dungeon
The NASA Workbench requires new schematics to craft higher tiers of rockets. These schematics are found in dungeons on planets in tier order. Tier 2 rocket schematics, for example, can be found in the reward room of Moon Dungeons. Dungeon entrances are deep holes on the surface that have unnatural brick blocks on the bottom.
The dungeons are naturally generated and so may be difficult to find. It is important to mark the location of each dungeon found as the coordinates are the same across each planet.
Higher tiers of rockets require different kinds of Rocket Fuels .

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Magic Mods
Chunk.text:
Magic Mods
IV is also the point at which much of the lategame content in many magic mods becomes available to players willing to invest into them.
In Thaumcraft , most of the Kami equipment that requires Ichor becomes available with Osmiridium, an alloy that is made from Osmium and Iridium and smelted in an LuV-tier EBF. This includes the best available wand materials, a set of powerful tools and armor, and the Pure Tear and Purification Talisman, both of which can be used to solve warp (the former once and the latter continuously). The Pure Tear can also be obtained through the Quest Book using one Osmiridium Ingot, which can help players struggling with warp who aren't close to obtaining Ichor and being able to craft it themselves.
In Blood Magic , the tier 5 and 6 Blood Orbs can be crafted once platline materials are obtained, which unlocks the ability to summon many more meteors and to reach almost all of the mod's content, including advanced rituals and spell parts. Furthermore, some of the most useful meteors require IV machines or components to summon, such as the IV Scanner meteor, which contains huge amounts of platline dusts.
In Botania , IV is the first tier where it's possible to summon the Gaia Guardian, although the naquadah that is required can make it challenging to afford until a later tier.

Chunk.title: Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Solar Panels
Solar panels are available in tiers from 1 EU/t all the way up to UV (524288 EU/t). Creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel (i.e. to make a LV panel you need to be HV). Solars are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, however they can nicely help your regular power gen, especially in operations that need to be running all the time or far away from your main power source.
Production: Solars up to ULV are crafted in the regular crafting grid, then in the Solar Factory multiblock. Panels are quite expensive to make up for not needing fuel, especially more so if you're making them without the previous solar panel.
Usage: Solar panels can be placed as a cover on a GT machine, battery buffer, machine hull or even cable, or crafted into a standalone solar panel block. Cover-type solars need periodic cleaning by right-clicking with empty hand while having a bucket of water in your inventory (can be done by golems), or their output will decrease. Solar panel blocks lack this disadvantage, also you don't need to protect them from rain.
Thaumcraft offers an option to make compressed solar panels. These take 8 panels of the previous tier to produce 10 times more power, so even if recipes become exponentially more expensive there's a bit of advantage. Octuple compressed solar panels can produce 100,000,000 EU/t, which is almost 200 times more than a UV solar panel. Moreover, there are infused versions of compressed solars which produce even more power under certain conditions. For example, octuple aqua infused solar can produce up to 600,000,000 EU/t while in thunderstorm. These also have the added bonus of being very TPS efficient, which is very important late game.
Starting from triple onwards, it will require infusion. Read the Infusion automation guide for help on automating these solars. The maximum tier is 8 (Octuple), and requires 16777216 1 volt solars. This spreadsheet lists all items needed to create an UV Solar Panel and an Octuple Compressed Solar. The sheet is outdated for the former, since it was made before solar factory was added.

Chunk.title: Ludicrous Voltage (LuV)
Chunk.text: Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) is the sixth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier is largely centered around building the infrastructure necessary to construct the first tier of Fusion Reactor , as well as the new items and machines gated by fusion. This is the first tier where the Assembly Line is used to craft on-tier components as well as highly advanced machines. In addition, the costs and crafting trees for machines are even larger than in previous tiers, making fully automated on-demand crafting with AE2 absolutely necessary. The massive demand for robust infrastructure continues for the rest of the game; arrays of Volcanus consuming on-tier voltage are highly suggested.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
Chunk.text: Insane Voltage (IV) is the fifth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, multiple new multiblocks and mechanics are introduced, such as the Assembly Line , the Precise Assembler , and many more. Chunk.text:
High Voltage (HV) is the third electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, several new mechanics are introduced to you such as cleanrooms , space travel , and multiblock versions of your singleblock machines. With the introduction of the Cleanroom, your ability to produce more complex circuits and some of their critical components will be restricted to the inside of the Cleanroom multiblock structure, or other multiblocks that are also considered cleanrooms. Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
Chunk.text:
GT Electric Machines
Machine GUI. Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.
LV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. Just like their Steam counterparts, all electric GT machines cannot be input or output from their front face. To enable automatic output, open the GUI of the machine and click on the button at the lower left corner. There are two automatic output toggle buttons; the left one is for liquid and the right one is for items.
Electrolyzer clay dust recipe. The MV power requirement is circled in yellow.
GregTech machinery is divided by tier, which corresponds to a specific voltage - LV (32 V), MV (128 V), HV (512 V) etc. Most recipes are gated to a specific voltage/tier or higher, which is shown with the recipe in NEI (Not Enough Items). If the recipe requires more than one amp it will also be listed here. Pay careful attention to what tier a recipe requires - with LV machinery, MV and higher recipes are inaccessible.
For example, putting Clay Dust through the Electrolyzer to get Aluminium dust requires 120 EU/t (MV). Since the Basic Electrolyzer is only able to do 32EU/t, this recipe is unavailable until the Advanced Electrolyzer (MV).
Recipes close to the voltage limit for LV (32 EU/t) may cause the machine to request multiple amps, especially if there is any cable loss. A single LV generator will often not be capable of supplying enough power if the machine is placed too far away. Most GT machines will accept up to 2 amps. A second generator or Battery Buffer may be needed to keep a a high cost recipe running. If a machine runs out of power, it will stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.
Some machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t

Chunk.title: Extreme Voltage (EV)
Chunk.text: Extreme Voltage (EV) is the fourth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, several mechanics are introduced such as Applied Energistics 2 (abbreviated as AE2) and the IndustrialCraft 2 Nuclear Reactors . This tier is largely centered around three big goals: starting an AE2 setup, traveling to Mars for new and important resources, and developing centralized electric infrastructure. It introduces several new multiblocks which greatly speed up many processes, but especially ore processing with the introduction of the Industrial Centrifuge , Industrial Maceration Stack , Ore Washing Plant , and others.

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
Chunk.text: Zero Point Voltage (ZPM) is the seventh electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier is largely centered around building the infrastructure necessary to construct the next tier of Fusion Reactor, which is necessary for progression into UV. In addition, this tier introduces TecTech, the source of many late game multi-blocks. It also sees additional power generation with the availability of the Large Naquadah Reactor and MK2 Fusion Controller, and a new source of resources in the Void Miner . However, similar to LuV, material costs and processing requirements continue to rise and so infrastructure such as a Mega Electric Blast Furnace , Mega Vacuum Freezer , and Mega Chemical Reactor may be necessary. Circuits get a major improvement with the addition of Europium-doped wafers. The PCB Factory is also build-able at this stage, though its quest is UV. ZPM is generally considered to mark the transition from midgame to lategame.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
Chunk.text:
Generation
In order to take full advantage of this power storage and distribution infrastructure, it is necessary for the player to also greatly expand their power generation, usually to hundreds of thousands of EU/t by the end of the tier. In order to accomplish this, IV unlocks a wealth of new power generation multiblocks, as well as processing multiblocks that greatly simplify the process of generating fuel, while also saving on power compared to their singleblock counterparts. Players using Benzene should upgrade to Nitrobenzene if they have not already, upgrade to better turbine materials such as HSS-S or HSS-E, and use new multiblocks like the Industrial Electrolyzer and Dangote Distillus . Players using oil can benefit from the Extreme Combustion Engine by upgrading to High-Octane Gasoline as their fuel, and can use the Dangote Distillus to improve the speed and efficiency of making that fuel. Nuclear Reactors remain a viable means of generating power as well, and players using steam gain access to the XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine to generate power from Superheated Steam more compactly. In addition, many unconventional means of power generation unlock in IV, such as the Deep Earth Heating Pump , Rocketdyne F-1A Engine , and Solar Tower .

Chunk.title: Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Steam
Steam is the first power source you have access to, and is the fuel for the first Bronze and Steel machines. Upon reaching LV , it is also the easiest way to generate EU, but boilers rapidly become less useful in the following tiers due to how difficult it becomes to transport a lot of Steam around to match the EU/t demands of your upgraded machines, especially your Electric Blast Furnace. After players centralise their power generation (usually around EV - IV) and no longer need to transport "fuel" around their base, Steam starts to become increasingly useful in power generation again, especially as they gain access to superheated, supercritical or dense variants of Steam.

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Power Generation
In ZPM, most existing power generation methods from earlier tiers, such as Nitrobenzene , Rocket Fuel, and Nuclear Reactors , remain viable, but start to fall off due to increasing power demands and a lack of upgrades. One notable upgrade is Huge Turbines for all gas, steam, or plasma-based power, which are unlocked with Americium.
Plasma, on the other hand, is still viable and will continue to be viable for many more tiers. In addition to the aforementioned Huge Turbines, plasma benefits from better fuels in the form of Tin Plasma or Runite Plasma (although the latter requires a UV Alloy Blast Smelter ), better production rates using the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, and the XL Plasma Turbine and XL Supercritical Steam Turbine to greatly improve power throughput.
A Large Naquadah Reactor.
ZPM also unlocks one of the strongest power generation methods in the mid and late game: Naquadah Fuel, often abbreviated to Naqfuel. Power is produced by inputting Naqfuel into a Large Naquadah Reactor (LNR), alongside Liquid Air, a coolant (Gelid Cryotheum), and an excited liquid (Molten Atomic Separation Catalyst), all of which will need to be produced in large quantities by players seeking to use the fuel for power. Two tiers of Naqfuel are available in ZPM: tier 1 requires the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, while tier 2 is produced by combining tier 1 fuel with a couple other ingredients in an overclocked Mega Chemical Reactor . Each LNR can generate up to 42.9M EU/t with Naqfuel 1, and up to 101.2M EU/t with Naqfuel 2.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
Chunk.text:
Rockets
Unlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station useful.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
section_paths: Low Voltage (LV) > Revisiting Steam > Steam Power Upgrades
Chunk.text:
Steam Power Upgrades
Up until LV your most automated options for generating Steam involved either regularly resetting Solar Boilers or collecting wood manually to feed Coke Ovens, the LV Crop Manager and tree bonsais allow for easy and cheap automation of Wood, enabling fully automatic power. Look into powering it with a semifluid generator directly with creosote, its a bit more power efficient and saves on pipe distance in most builds. You can try and breed the bonsais for max stats but that won't be necessary, even one 11x11 layer of 1/1/1 bonsais will provide more than enough wood for a max size RC Boiler . Speaking of RC boilers, the tank recipe gets substantially cheaper in LV, with the screw requirement being dropped with the assembler; the casing required for the tanks can also be made cheaper by utilising the Bender and the Cutting Machine.
After visiting the Twilight Forest, the player can utilise the lead found to make Potin fluid pipes, which offer substantially more throughput than Bronze pipes of the same size. You can utilise the Fluid Extractor and Solidifier to produce pipes substantially quicker than with the Bender.

Chunk.title: Power Generation
section_paths: Power Generation > Steam > Production > Later Tier Steam Production
Chunk.text:
Later Tier Steam Production
In later tiers, large quantities of Supercritical or Superheated Steam can be produced by a Large Heat Exchanger fed by hot fluids like lava or hot coolant, which is able to be produced infinitely in several ways (e.g Everburn Urns from Thaumcraft). Another way to get Superheated Steam is through the Large Titanium Boiler and Large Tungstensteel Boiler, but run only with more specific fuels (like Solid Super Fuels). This continues into the endgame, with Dense Supercritical Steam being provided by an Extreme Heat Exchanger . Many mid- to late-game power generation options use steam in some capacity, whether directly, or via a heat exchanger (e.g. the Fusion Reactor , Solar Tower Fluid Reactors , DEHP , Solid-Oxide Fuel Cells , HTGR , LFTR , THTR ).

Chunk.title: Electricity
Chunk.text:
Cables and Loss
GregTech EU can be transferred using GregTech Cables.
Rather than priority by destination, power priority is given by cardinal direction. Cables will push power in the following priority:
- Down
- Up
- North
- South
- West
- East
When producing power, each generator will always attempt to empty all of its internal buffer at once. This can cause one generator in a cable network to use fuel more rapidly than another, with order depending on tile entity processing and changing on chunk reloads.
All GT Cables have a max Voltage, max Amperage and a Loss/Meter/Ampere, indicated on their tooltip:
- Cables which receive amps containing more EU than their maximum Voltage will catch fire and melt.
- Cables that have more amps travelling through them than their maximum Amperage limit will catch fire and melt. Note that machines can request more Amperage than strictly required by their active recipe.
- Each energy packet travelling through a cable loses Voltage per block travelled. The amount of EU lost is indicated by the Loss/Meter/Ampere number.
Each Material has 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x uninsulated Wires. Most of these have cable variants, except for the superconductor wires, as well as graphene, Ichorium, hypogen, Black Plutonium, Awakened Draconium, Infinity, and SpaceTime wires. Note that Uninsulated Wires have twice the Loss/Meter/Ampere as Insulated Cables. The only exceptions to this are Red alloy and Redstone alloy (as their cables are lossless, while the wires are not), Quantium, Lumiium, and Signalium (four times the loss when uninsulated), and Bedrockium (8x loss when uninsulated).
For example:
- A 1x Tin Cable can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 1 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. This means that 1 amp can travel 32 blocks before it dies.
- A 1x Tin Wire can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 2 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. In this case, the amp can travel 16 blocks only.

Chunk.text:
Steam
Steam is the first power source you have access to, and is the fuel for the first Bronze and Steel machines. Upon reaching LV , it is also the easiest way to generate EU, but boilers rapidly become less useful in the following tiers due to how difficult it becomes to transport a lot of Steam around to match the EU/t demands of your upgraded machines, especially your Electric Blast Furnace. Chunk.text:
Later Tier Steam Production
In later tiers, large quantities of Supercritical or Superheated Steam can be produced by a Large Heat Exchanger fed by hot fluids like lava or hot coolant, which is able to be produced infinitely in several ways (e.g Everburn Urns from Thaumcraft). Chunk.text:
Blast Off \O/
You did it! You crafted your first rocket ever in this modpack. Now you need to fuel it with 5 cells worth of cetane-boosted diesel. Note that rocket will produce a huge amount of pollution if launched. When you land, you should find yourself in a lander. YOU MUST HOLD THE SPACE BAR (or you will die and lose your rocket) to slow down the lander. You should keep your descent velocity to less than 20 m/s to avoid exploding yourself on landing. Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Power Generation
In ZPM, most existing power generation methods from earlier tiers, such as Nitrobenzene , Rocket Fuel, and Nuclear Reactors , remain viable, but start to fall off due to increasing power demands and a lack of upgrades. One notable upgrade is Huge Turbines for all gas, steam, or plasma-based power, which are unlocked with Americium.
Plasma, on the other hand, is still viable and will continue to be viable for many more tiers. In addition to the aforementioned Huge Turbines, plasma benefits from better fuels in the form of Tin Plasma or Runite Plasma (although the latter requires a UV Alloy Blast Smelter ), better production rates using the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, and the XL Plasma Turbine and XL Supercritical Steam Turbine to greatly improve power throughput.
A Large Naquadah Reactor.
ZPM also unlocks one of the strongest power generation methods in the mid and late game: Naquadah Fuel, often abbreviated to Naqfuel. Power is produced by inputting Naqfuel into a Large Naquadah Reactor (LNR), alongside Liquid Air, a coolant (Gelid Cryotheum), and an excited liquid (Molten Atomic Separation Catalyst), all of which will need to be produced in large quantities by players seeking to use the fuel for power. Two tiers of Naqfuel are available in ZPM: tier 1 requires the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, while tier 2 is produced by combining tier 1 fuel with a couple other ingredients in an overclocked Mega Chemical Reactor . Each LNR can generate up to 42.9M EU/t with Naqfuel 1, and up to 101.2M EU/t with Naqfuel 2.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Power
UV is the point at which power generation from the early game falls off: Nitrobenzene, Rocket Fuel, and Nuclear Reactors can last up to this point, but should be replaced by the start of the next tier. Plasma or Naquadah Fuel, both of which are viable in UV and able to scale for multiple more tiers, should be used instead. Plasma gains access to the Fusion Reactor Mk3, which provides both access to the best plasma chain fuels and an overclock on earlier fusion recipes to reduce the need for spam, and the Stocking Input Hatch helps parallelize on slower fusion steps. It also benefits from new better turbine materials, such as Cosmic Neutronium. Naquadah Fuel also benefits from these improvements for its slow fusion step, and gains access to Haumea Void Miners , the Space Elevator, and the Mega Apiary to help source its inputs.

Chunk.text:
Generation
In order to take full advantage of this power storage and distribution infrastructure, it is necessary for the player to also greatly expand their power generation, usually to hundreds of thousands of EU/t by the end of the tier. In order to accomplish this, IV unlocks a wealth of new power generation multiblocks, as well as processing multiblocks that greatly simplify the process of generating fuel, while also saving on power compared to their singleblock counterparts. Players using Benzene should upgrade to Nitrobenzene if they have not already, upgrade to better turbine materials such as HSS-S or HSS-E, and use new multiblocks like the Industrial Electrolyzer and Dangote Distillus . Players using oil can benefit from the Extreme Combustion Engine by upgrading to High-Octane Gasoline as their fuel, and can use the Dangote Distillus to improve the speed and efficiency of making that fuel. Nuclear Reactors remain a viable means of generating power as well, and players using steam gain access to the XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine to generate power from Superheated Steam more compactly. In addition, many unconventional means of power generation unlock in IV, such as the Deep Earth Heating Pump , Rocketdyne F-1A Engine , and Solar Tower .

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
section_paths: Low Voltage (LV) > Revisiting Steam > Steam Power Upgrades
Chunk.text:
Steam Power Upgrades
Up until LV your most automated options for generating Steam involved either regularly resetting Solar Boilers or collecting wood manually to feed Coke Ovens, the LV Crop Manager and tree bonsais allow for easy and cheap automation of Wood, enabling fully automatic power. You can try and breed the bonsais for max stats but that won't be necessary, even one 11x11 layer of 1/1/1 bonsais will provide more than enough wood for a max size RC Boiler . Speaking of RC boilers, the tank recipe gets substantially cheaper in LV, with the screw requirement being dropped with the assembler; the casing required for the tanks can also be made cheaper by utilising the Bender and the Cutting Machine.
After visiting the Twilight Forest, the player can utilise the lead found to make Potin fluid pipes, which offer substantially more throughput than Bronze pipes of the same size. You can utilise the Fluid Extractor and Solidifier to produce pipes substantially quicker than with the Bender.

Chunk.title: Planets
Chunk.text:
The Galaxy Map of the Solar System.
There are many different planets, asteroid belts, and star systems within GTNH. To reach them, launch a rocket into space and select a destination on the galaxy map. Some destinations (e.g. moons and space stations) only appear when zoomed into the host planet's orbit. Confirming the location then instantly teleports you to the planet at some very high altitude and inside a lander that carries you down to the surface. The rocket and launch pads are retrieved from the lander upon a complete stop, but sometimes it bugs out and never fully stops. If that happens, place a hopper underneath the lander to retrieve the items. Later on, use the Space Elevator to travel to other planets without any rocket fuel.
The tier of a planet (visible in NEI ) determines the minimum tier rocket needed to travel there. For example, a T2 rocket or better is required to reach any T2 planet, such as Mars. There are 8 tiers of rockets in total so the only way to reach the last tier of planets (T9) in the Amun-Ra system is with a Mothership .
Every planet has its own set of ore veins, small ore veins, and underground fluid reservoirs (visible in NEI ). Some planets also have unique features such as a specific mob that spawns, a Space Dungeon , or even abandoned structures from past civilizations. The following sections lists all relevant information for every planet with certain items highlighted BLUE to signify high importance or value (e.g. a new ore vein). Note that some planets are gas giants which means a space station must be built in their orbit before using the Planetary Gas Siphon to extract their resources.

Chunk.text:
Crafting Tier 2+ Rockets
Entrance to a Moon Dungeon
The NASA Workbench requires new schematics to craft higher tiers of rockets. These schematics are found in dungeons on planets in tier order. Tier 2 rocket schematics, for example, can be found in the reward room of Moon Dungeons. Dungeon entrances are deep holes on the surface that have unnatural brick blocks on the bottom.
The dungeons are naturally generated and so may be difficult to find. It is important to mark the location of each dungeon found as the coordinates are the same across each planet.
Higher tiers of rockets require different kinds of Rocket Fuels .

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Tier 7 Rocket
The Tier 7 Rocket is available as soon as the player is able to power their Assembly Line with two UV Energy Hatches to overclock it to UHV. section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Power Generation
In ZPM, most existing power generation methods from earlier tiers, such as Nitrobenzene , Rocket Fuel, and Nuclear Reactors , remain viable, but start to fall off due to increasing power demands and a lack of upgrades. One notable upgrade is Huge Turbines for all gas, steam, or plasma-based power, which are unlocked with Americium.
Plasma, on the other hand, is still viable and will continue to be viable for many more tiers. In addition to the aforementioned Huge Turbines, plasma benefits from better fuels in the form of Tin Plasma or Runite Plasma (although the latter requires a UV Alloy Blast Smelter ), better production rates using the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, and the XL Plasma Turbine and XL Supercritical Steam Turbine to greatly improve power throughput.
A Large Naquadah Reactor.
ZPM also unlocks one of the strongest power generation methods in the mid and late game: Naquadah Fuel, often abbreviated to Naqfuel. Power is produced by inputting Naqfuel into a Large Naquadah Reactor (LNR), alongside Liquid Air, a coolant (Gelid Cryotheum), and an excited liquid (Molten Atomic Separation Catalyst), all of which will need to be produced in large quantities by players seeking to use the fuel for power. Two tiers of Naqfuel are available in ZPM: tier 1 requires the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, while tier 2 is produced by combining tier 1 fuel with a couple other ingredients in an overclocked Mega Chemical Reactor . Each LNR can generate up to 42.9M EU/t with Naqfuel 1, and up to 101.2M EU/t with Naqfuel 2.

Chunk.title: Extreme Voltage (EV)
section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Energy crisis - part 1
Chunk.text:
Energy crisis - part 1
You might've found you are struggling to power up those EV single block machines with just several HV generators (either automated or not). If your main energy production is from oil, it's recommended to build a multiblock combustion engine and upgrade to cetane-boosted diesel if you didn't in HV. It costs about 4 stacks of titanium to make and without boosting with oxygen, produces 2048EU/t at 100% efficiency, and if boosted with oxygen, produces 6144EU/t at 150% efficiency. Because of the boosting mechanism, it's recommended to keep it boosting. It also requires a small amount of lubricant to run.
Another option is large gas turbine. It runs at efficiency based on the turbine you put into the controller. The gas input must be close to the optimal flow rate the turbine describes, or efficiency will drop. There is also a replacement, the oxidation fuel unit, where it's the same but does not need a turbine but needs oxygen to run but produces steam, but it's not recommended because it only produces 2048EU/t while costing more than the gas turbine. Also, its efficiency caps at 100% while large gas turbines are based on the turbine and can easily go beyond 100% efficiency.
If you want to make platline or got some platinum, you can build your first nuclear generator. You can check the Nuclear Reactor page to find what design that fits best for you. I recommend you to use the 1280EU/t design as it only needs 4 chambers (3 chambers for the main block). Build as many as you need as the reactor is pretty cheap in both maintaining and its build cost.

Chunk.text:
Power
UV is the point at which power generation from the early game falls off: Nitrobenzene, Rocket Fuel, and Nuclear Reactors can last up to this point, but should be replaced by the start of the next tier. Plasma or Naquadah Fuel, both of which are viable in UV and able to scale for multiple more tiers, should be used instead. Plasma gains access to the Fusion Reactor Mk3, which provides both access to the best plasma chain fuels and an overclock on earlier fusion recipes to reduce the need for spam, and the Stocking Input Hatch helps parallelize on slower fusion steps. It also benefits from new better turbine materials, such as Cosmic Neutronium. Naquadah Fuel also benefits from these improvements for its slow fusion step, and gains access to Haumea Void Miners , the Space Elevator, and the Mega Apiary to help source its inputs.

Chunk.text:
Power
The Eye of Harmony is extremely power-hungry, and will likely consume most of the player's power generation while they progress through its tiers. Without any overclocks its power usage is fairly modest, on the order of 100B EU/t, but it is also extremely slow, and adding even a single overclock increases it to multiple trillion EU/t due to its very inefficient overclocks. In UMV, there are three viable sources of power to run the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure.

Chunk.title: Power Generation
Chunk.text:
Enriched Naquadah/Naquadria Reactors
See More: Large Naquadah Reactor and Naquadah Fuel Refinery
Singleblock naquadah reactors produce large amounts of power at a constant eu/t, as stated on the machine's tooltip. These drain power depending by depleting tiberium/enriched naquadah/naquadria screw/rods/long rods into normal naquadah screws/rods/long rods, converting it into an internal buffer that is drained at a constant eu/t. The efficiency of the machine multiplies the EU potential of the rod, giving the true energy per item. They are best for remote mining drills and should not be used as a main source of power.
The Large Naquadah Reactor (LNR) is much different from the singleblock reactors. Instead of rods, it consumes nuclear based fuels for breeding and naquadah based fuels for power generation. There are six tiers of naquadah fuel: MK1 and MK2 fuels are made in a fusion reactor while MK3 and above are made in the Naquadah Fuel Refinery , a multiblock available late into UHV. The LNR requires liquid air to function and optionally can be supplied with o ne type of coolant and one type of booster to further improve power output. Coolants increase the efficiency of the naquadah based fuels (IC2 coolant: 105% efficiency, super coolant: 150% efficiency, Cryotheum: 275%, and Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid: 500%). Boosters increase both the fuel consumption and output of the reactor (molten caesium: 2x, molten U-235: 3x, molten naquadah: 4x, molten atomic separation catalyst: 16x, and spatially enlarged fluid: 64x).
The LNR is much better than plasma turbines because there is no turbine durability to worry about, higher power output, and less space required.

section_paths: Extremely Ultimate Voltage (UEV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Power > Generation
Chunk.text:
Generation
Naquadah Fuel and Plasma remain the only viable power sources in UEV. Naqfuel can be upgraded to Mk4, or even Mk5, by using Tier 2 coils in the Naquadah Fuel Refinery and combining Mk3 fuel with various materials. Prior to the DTPF, only the weaker recipes for both fuels are viable, but the DTPF can be used to produce Hypogen and Infinity fast enough to use the stronger recipes, improving the efficiency of Mk3 fuel. Plasma gains access to the Compact 4 to increase fuel production, but Infinity remains the best available rotor material.

Chunk.title: Electricity
Chunk.text:
Overclocking
Main Article: Overclocking
Machines of higher tiers can receive overclocks to speed up their recipes.
Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and total EU consumption, leading to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, overclocking is also called 2/4 overclocking.
A perfect overclock instead quadruples the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same. This still leads to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, perfect overclocking is also called 4/4 overclocking.
Machines typically receive one overclock per voltage tier above the minimum required for a recipe.
Singleblock machines can only ever regular overclock.
Multiblock machines perfect overclock on a case-by-case basis; their tooltips contain information on how to achieve perfect overclocks or upgrade overclocks to perfect overclocks. If no information is mentioned, they will regular overclock.
Multiblocks with two energy hatches of the same voltage will always draw 4A to overclock a recipe to a tier higher than the energy hatch voltage (since 4A of the lower voltage contains the same EU as 1A of the higher voltage). This also allows them to run recipes with a minimum requirement of that higher voltage tier.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
Chunk.text:
Energy Loss
The tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible.

First Energy Crisis
You may find yourself struggling to power HV EBFs and possibly even your singleblock machines for long periods of time, as each HV machine you make consumes 4x (not accounting for efficiency loss) the amount of fuel compared to your MV generators. You should expand and fully automate your energy production setup.
In HV, combustion generators gain a massive buff thanks to the addition of Cetane-Boosted Diesel, which boasts a whopping 1M EU per cell, a massive expansion over Diesel. In addition, Benzene is heavily improved thanks to the Distillation Tower and Pyrolyse Oven coil upgrades which significantly speed up Benzene production. The Distillation Tower will even produce Phenol and Toluene which can be burned in Gas Turbines if you're in a pinch. Note that these infrastructure upgrades require significant amounts of resources upfront, but the infrastructure investment easily carries over into EV.

Chunk.title: Electricity
Chunk.text:
Amperage
In code, amps are pushed, not pulled. However, they are only pushed when requested by machines. Thus, for all scopes except pack development, you can assume amps are only ever pulled as needed.
Machines and energy hatches draw amps to fill their internal EU buffers. The capacity of the internal buffer is listed as "Capacity:" in the machine's or hatch's tooltip. When processing a recipe, a machine will draw from its internal buffer. The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .
The maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left\lfloor {\frac {2\times {\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\right\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Recipe amperages listed in NEI are a recommended number to fill the internal buffer at a rate that breaks even against usage.
Several common amperages of GregTech machines can be found in the table below. "Drawing" means "draws up to", unless otherwise stated.
Output amps contain the maximum EU for the outputting machine's voltage tier.
Machine | Notes
Machine: Singleblock Generators | Notes: Output 1A of its tier
Machine: Energy Hatches | Notes: Draws 2A (second amp mostly for extra draw for loss)
Machine: Step-up Transformers | Notes: Draws 4A lower voltage, outputs 1A higher voltage
Machine: Step-down Transformers | Notes: Draws 1A higher voltage, outputs 4A lower voltage
Machine: Battery Buffers | Notes: Draws 2A per Battery, outputs 1A per Battery.
Machine: Battery Chargers | Notes: Draws 4-8A per Battery, outputs 2-4A per Battery correspondingly.
Machine: Arc Furnace | Notes: Most recipes require 3A to break even against EU/t usage
Machine: Thermal Centrifuge | Notes: Most recipes require 2A to break even against EU/t usage

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
Chunk.text:
EU (Energy Units) Mechanics
GregTech energy consists of Voltage and Amperage. A Low Voltage (LV) GT generator will output 32 volts (32V) in 1 amperage (1A/1 amp). Four generators on the same cable will output 32 volts in 4 amps combined. 32 volts in 4 amps is not the same thing as MV (Medium Voltage - 128 volts per amp). This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. Picture of a Transformer in default mode transferring 1 amp of HV into 4 amps of MV.
Transformers convert EU between voltage tiers. Chunk.text:
Graviton Shards
The Stargate requires 512 Graviton Shards, which can be ejected from the Godforge after completing its final upgrade, END. After unlocking Inversion by reaching level 7 on each milestone, it becomes possible to scale the milestones infinitely to produce enough shards. Each of the four milestones can be pushed in order to rapidly gain shards, although it is more efficient to prioritize one or two milestones due to the fact that the number of shards gained scales quadratically, while the requirements only scale linearly. Charge can be pushed by using the unlimited maximum voltage unlocked by the TBF upgrade, Conversion by running a cheap recipe such as steel and re-macerating it repeatedly, Catalyst by using MHDCSM with a high fuel factor, and Composition by placing more Heliofusion Exoticizers in Magmatter mode.

Chunk.title: Planets
Chunk.text:
The Galaxy Map of the Solar System.
There are many different planets, asteroid belts, and star systems within GTNH. To reach them, launch a rocket into space and select a destination on the galaxy map. Some destinations (e.g. moons and space stations) only appear when zoomed into the host planet's orbit. The following sections lists all relevant information for every planet with certain items highlighted BLUE to signify high importance or value (e.g. a new ore vein). Chunk.title: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV)
Chunk.text:
Mothership
The Mothership is the end of UHV progression, being required to reach Tier 9 planets and obtain Tengam, the magnetic material in UEV through UMV motors. Creating a Mothership requires launching a Shuttle Rocket while holding the necessary blocks and items, similar to a space station. The Shuttle Rocket's schematic is not found in a dungeon like previous schematics, but is instead crafted in the Assembly Line. Once the Mothership is built, engines must be placed on it and provided with fuel to travel to the Amun-Ra system, which contains the six Tier 9 planets; the only relevant to unlock UEV is Seth, which contains Tengam, as the Space Elevator is a better source of everything else on these planets. A small amount of dilithium from Neper is useful early in UEV. The Space Elevator can be used to travel to them, but only after obtaining MK-III motors, which require the DTPF. The Mothership also requires many previously optional steps in progression, such as the Nano Forge , Radox, and Kevlar.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text: Ultimate Voltage (UV) is the eighth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. It is largely centered around the new Wetware circuit line, which introduces new multiblocks like the Quantum Computer and Research Station , as well a-s the new technologies that are unlocked with them, like the third tier of Fusion Reactor . It also introduces many multiblocks for improving infrastructure, including the Mega Alloy Blast Smelter , Component Assembly Line , and Space Elevator , as well as key automation tools like the Stocking Input Hatch.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Tier 7 Rocket
The Tier 7 Rocket is available as soon as the player is able to power their Assembly Line with two UV Energy Hatches to overclock it to UHV. It unlocks four new planets: Haumea, Makemake, Pluto, and the Kuiper Belt, which should only be mined using Void Miners at this point. The most useful planet to mine is Haumea, which has the earliest source of Nether Star Ore as well as a high chance for Infused Gold Ore, making it very useful for setting up the second tier of Naquadah Fuel. Other new ores are Borax, Red Garnet, Yellow Garnet, and Chrysotile. The available underground fluids are Hydrofluoric Acid on Makemake, and Oxygen, Nitrogen, Fluorine, and Liquid Air on Pluto.
The dungeons containing the next tier of schematic are found on Pluto, alongside the Draconic Core Schematic for the Draconic Evolution Fusion Crafter . It is highly recommended to place the Tier 8 Rocket Schematic in a singleblock Scanner (a Research Station in Scanner mode will not work) and duplicate it using a UV Circuit Assembler, because two Tier 8 Rocket Schematics will be needed: one for making the Tier 8 Rocket, and one to be researched for the Shuttle Schematic for the Mothership .

Storage Rockets
In the T1 Rocket craft, there is an optional slot below the rocket control computer to add a copper, iron, or gold chest into (these recipes are also available in NEI ). This will add storage space to the rocket, but it will not be detected by the T1 Rocket quest in the Space Race tab. These can be converted to the normal rocket in a crafting grid.

Chunk.title: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV)
Chunk.text: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) is the ninth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. It unlocks Bioprocessors, infinity ingots, and Draconic Evolution. The overall goal is the construction of the Mothership and Shuttle rocket to reach the Amun-Ra system, which is required to get your foot through the door of UEV . In UHV, many previously optional processing chains and multiblocks become necessary for progression.

Chunk.title: Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage (UXV)
Chunk.text: Welcome to Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage (UXV) the thirteenth and final tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier begins with the production of Magnetohydrodynamically Constrained Star Matter (MHDCSM) and ends with a Stargate . In UXV, expect to spam even more machines and drastically increase power production to support laser energy hatches.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Space Elevator
A Space Elevator.
The Space Elevator is a modular multiblock that can be made late in UV, after obtaining UHV circuits. Although it supports many different modules with various abilities, the only one obtainable in UV is the first tier of Space Mining Module, which can produce hundreds or thousands of ores per second using a non-consumed tiered mining drone, computation from a Quantum Computer , rods and drill tips of varying materials depending on the mining drone, and Helium, Bismuth, or Radon Plasma. It can also be configured to change the available ores and modify the chances of each ore being produced. Using the Space Elevator effectively requires robust ore processing, including any processing lines like the Platline or Naqline whose inputs come from ores, and sufficient automatic production of plasma and rods/drill tips of the relevant material. Although it is available in UV, it is expensive enough and available late enough in the tier that many players do not build it until UHV.
The Space Elevator can also be used to travel to any planet up to Tier 8, although it cannot be used to return, so it's necessary to bring a rocket or other means of teleportation to get back. This mechanic can be used to reach Tier 8 planets without the Tier 8 Rocket, and thereby gain earlier access to materials like Awakened Draconium and Infinity Catalyst. An upgrade to Tier 3 motors unlocks travel to Tier 9 planets in UIV.

Tier 8 Rocket
This is the last regular rocket upgrade. Tier 8 plate ingots need two UHV energy hatches in the assembly line. The rocket unlocks multiple exoplanets. There is no new dungeon, the Shuttle Rocket schematic can be crafted using a schematic from a Pluto dungeon.
- T Ceti E is required for seaweed, which is used for the new circuit line. A few stacks might be needed to extract the culture.
- Barnarda C is the only source of Unknown Liquid before UEV, and the trees are needed to manufacture Xenoxene.
- Vega B has Infinity Catalyst as a small ore, although meteors are an alternative that is available slightly earlier.

section_paths: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) > Sidequests > Old Stargate Trophies
Chunk.text:
Old Stargate Trophies
UHV contains the first of four old Stargate quests in the Quest Book . These quests are entirely optional, and require submitting the materials needed to make two stargates in an older version of GTNH in order to complete the quest and receive a trophy. Each quest also provides context about the features available and the history of the Stargate during its version. The UHV old Stargate, also known as the Stargate of Split Origin, corresponds to version 2.1.0.0. Although it is the cheapest of the four old Stargates, it is still incredibly expensive by the standards of UHV. Among other ingredients, it requires 625 Eternal Singularities, 41k Bio Mainframes, 233k Infinity, 5.3M UHV Superconductor, and 2.1M Tritanium. As a result, it is best done in later tiers.

section_paths: Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Component Assembly Line
Chunk.text:
Component Assembly Line
The Component Assembly Line (CoAL) is a new multiblock for assembling components, such as Electric Motors, Robot Arms, and Sensors. It provides a 25% discount on both resources and time, as well as skipping the Assembly Line , two incredible advantages that mean it should be the only source of components whenever it can be used. The main cost of the CoAL is the 43 tiered Component Assembly Line Casings that determine the maximum available tier of components: a full CoAL takes 688 Electric Motors, 430 Electric Pistons, and 344 Robot Arms of its tier. Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)

Rockets

Chunk.text:
Preparation for making the rocket
You need a NASA workbench and a Implosion Compressor for your first rocket. You will find that the NASA Workbench is a particularly arduous craft that for some reason requires you to use GT tools in a crafting grid in HV. On the other hand, the Implosion Compressor should be trivial for the average player, regardless of setup.
The amount of explosives needed for use with the Implosion Compressor is non-trivial, though. You will be expending several stacks of TNT. If your energy setup is based on benzene, you will find that obtaining enough toluene for TNT will be trivial if you upgrade your setup to use a Distillation Tower instead of single-block distilleries. However, if your energy setup is based on oil, you will need some additional processing steps-- diverting some Heavy Fuel for use in a distillery or Distillation Tower will likely be the best way.
You'll need 37 T1 heavy-duty alloy plates and a ton of additional materials. Check the quest book. You'll need a T1 rocket, an oxygen equipment set with 2 light oxygen tanks (only 1 is very risky for resource collecting), an oxygen collector and compressor, a fuel loader, and 9 landing pads.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Tier 7 Rocket
The Tier 7 Rocket is available as soon as the player is able to power their Assembly Line with two UV Energy Hatches to overclock it to UHV. It unlocks four new planets: Haumea, Makemake, Pluto, and the Kuiper Belt, which should only be mined using Void Miners at this point. The most useful planet to mine is Haumea, which has the earliest source of Nether Star Ore as well as a high chance for Infused Gold Ore, making it very useful for setting up the second tier of Naquadah Fuel. Other new ores are Borax, Red Garnet, Yellow Garnet, and Chrysotile. The available underground fluids are Hydrofluoric Acid on Makemake, and Oxygen, Nitrogen, Fluorine, and Liquid Air on Pluto.
The dungeons containing the next tier of schematic are found on Pluto, alongside the Draconic Core Schematic for the Draconic Evolution Fusion Crafter . It is highly recommended to place the Tier 8 Rocket Schematic in a singleblock Scanner (a Research Station in Scanner mode will not work) and duplicate it using a UV Circuit Assembler, because two Tier 8 Rocket Schematics will be needed: one for making the Tier 8 Rocket, and one to be researched for the Shuttle Schematic for the Mothership .

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
Chunk.text: Insane Voltage (IV) is the fifth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, multiple new multiblocks and mechanics are introduced, such as the Assembly Line , the Precise Assembler , and many more. This is also the tier where many parts of magic (Thaumcraft, etc.) are unlocked for players to use; however, as always, watch your warp effects if you have been getting warp. While transitioning from the old tier to a new tier is usually the hard part, the IV tier is by far the hardest tier to get through. If you managed to get through EV tier, prepare yourself because this tier requires a very heavy transition in almost every aspect of your base, including infrastructure and crafting. At this point, manual crafting is no longer a feasible option. With this being said, be prepared for a big change to your base!

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
Chunk.text:
High Voltage (HV) is the third electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, several new mechanics are introduced to you such as cleanrooms , space travel , and multiblock versions of your singleblock machines. With the introduction of the Cleanroom, your ability to produce more complex circuits and some of their critical components will be restricted to the inside of the Cleanroom multiblock structure, or other multiblocks that are also considered cleanrooms. Many important materials, such as titanium, can only be extracted from ores that exist on other planets and celestial bodies. You will find that all of these mechanics will carry on with you for the foreseeable future.
Upon reaching HV, you should either have the ability to produce large quantities of stainless steel or quickly plan on developing the infrastructure to do so, as this is the first tier that starts demanding large quantities of its respective machine hull material, whether it's through the numerous single block machines or new multi-block machines such as the expensive but rewarding Distillation Tower.

Chunk.text:
Graviton Shards
The Stargate requires 512 Graviton Shards, which can be ejected from the Godforge after completing its final upgrade, END. After unlocking Inversion by reaching level 7 on each milestone, it becomes possible to scale the milestones infinitely to produce enough shards. Each of the four milestones can be pushed in order to rapidly gain shards, although it is more efficient to prioritize one or two milestones due to the fact that the number of shards gained scales quadratically, while the requirements only scale linearly. Charge can be pushed by using the unlimited maximum voltage unlocked by the TBF upgrade, Conversion by running a cheap recipe such as steel and re-macerating it repeatedly, Catalyst by using MHDCSM with a high fuel factor, and Composition by placing more Heliofusion Exoticizers in Magmatter mode.

This is the first tier where the Assembly Line is used to craft on-tier components as well as highly advanced machines. In addition, the costs and crafting trees for machines are even larger than in previous tiers, making fully automated on-demand crafting with AE2 absolutely necessary. The massive demand for robust infrastructure continues for the rest of the game; arrays of Volcanus consuming on-tier voltage are highly suggested.

Tier 8 Rocket
This is the last regular rocket upgrade. Tier 8 plate ingots need two UHV energy hatches in the assembly line. The rocket unlocks multiple exoplanets. There is no new dungeon, the Shuttle Rocket schematic can be crafted using a schematic from a Pluto dungeon.
- T Ceti E is required for seaweed, which is used for the new circuit line. A few stacks might be needed to extract the culture.
- Barnarda C is the only source of Unknown Liquid before UEV, and the trees are needed to manufacture Xenoxene.
- Vega B has Infinity Catalyst as a small ore, although meteors are an alternative that is available slightly earlier.
- Barnarda F has Bedrockium as a small ore. While not strictly required, it is a good source for the required large-scale production.

Preparation for making the rocket
You need a NASA workbench and a Implosion Compressor for your first rocket. You will find that the NASA Workbench is a particularly arduous craft that for some reason requires you to use GT tools in a crafting grid in HV. On the other hand, the Implosion Compressor should be trivial for the average player, regardless of setup.
The amount of explosives needed for use with the Implosion Compressor is non-trivial, though. You will be expending several stacks of TNT. If your energy setup is based on benzene, you will find that obtaining enough toluene for TNT will be trivial if you upgrade your setup to use a Distillation Tower instead of single-block distilleries. However, if your energy setup is based on oil, you will need some additional processing steps-- diverting some Heavy Fuel for use in a distillery or Distillation Tower will likely be the best way.
You'll need 37 T1 heavy-duty alloy plates and a ton of additional materials. Check the quest book. You'll need a T1 rocket, an oxygen equipment set with 2 light oxygen tanks (only 1 is very risky for resource collecting), an oxygen collector and compressor, a fuel loader, and 9 landing pads.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Launch Process
During the 20-second ignition period, the rocket produces 100 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 100\times Tier}} pollution/sec and will begin to shake and emit white smoke particles. After the launch begins, the launchpads will break, and the rocket will fly straight up without player steering. While the rocket is flying, it will produce 10000 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 10000\times Tier}} pollution/sec. Note that due to a bug the rocket will actually emit 20x that amount of pollution in version prior to 2.9. A GUI indicator on the left side of the screen will display the rocket's height relative to the world. If the rocket hits any blocks, it will stall and waste fuel, requiring player steering. If a rocket runs out of fuel while launching, it will explode.
Upon reaching maximum height (y~1100 for the overworld), the player will be transported away from their current dimension and be shown a catalog of solar systems and planets. Clicking on a planet allows the player to build a Space Station there or launch there as the destination on the upper right hand side. Clicking on the planet again will zoom in on it and display its moons and space stations, which can also be launched to. The tier requirement of a launch is listed on the top of the screen; insufficient tier requirements prevent selecting a planet as a destination. The available destinations only depend on the tier of the rocket, not on the launch site.
Upon selecting a destination, the destination will be loaded in, and the player will descend riding some form of a Lunar Lander (Parachute, Lunar Lander, Landing Balloons, etc.). For the Moon , the player must press space to expend fuel and slow down the Lunar Lander to a descent rate slower than -20m/s to prevent an explosive crash landing. Upon landing, the player can exit the Lander by sneaking. The Lunar Lander will hold the rocket (with its fuel) and launchpads, used for a return flight. Punch to break it like a boat.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Crafting Tier 2+ Rockets
Entrance to a Moon Dungeon
The NASA Workbench requires new schematics to craft higher tiers of rockets. These schematics are found in dungeons on planets in tier order. Tier 2 rocket schematics, for example, can be found in the reward room of Moon Dungeons. Dungeon entrances are deep holes on the surface that have unnatural brick blocks on the bottom.
The dungeons are naturally generated and so may be difficult to find. It is important to mark the location of each dungeon found as the coordinates are the same across each planet.
Higher tiers of rockets require different kinds of Rocket Fuels .

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
Chunk.text:
Tier 7 Rocket
The Tier 7 Rocket is available as soon as the player is able to power their Assembly Line with two UV Energy Hatches to overclock it to UHV. It unlocks four new planets: Haumea, Makemake, Pluto, and the Kuiper Belt, which should only be mined using Void Miners at this point. The most useful planet to mine is Haumea, which has the earliest source of Nether Star Ore as well as a high chance for Infused Gold Ore, making it very useful for setting up the second tier of Naquadah Fuel. Other new ores are Borax, Red Garnet, Yellow Garnet, and Chrysotile. The available underground fluids are Hydrofluoric Acid on Makemake, and Oxygen, Nitrogen, Fluorine, and Liquid Air on Pluto.
The dungeons containing the next tier of schematic are found on Pluto, alongside the Draconic Core Schematic for the Draconic Evolution Fusion Crafter . It is highly recommended to place the Tier 8 Rocket Schematic in a singleblock Scanner (a Research Station in Scanner mode will not work) and duplicate it using a UV Circuit Assembler, because two Tier 8 Rocket Schematics will be needed: one for making the Tier 8 Rocket, and one to be researched for the Shuttle Schematic for the Mothership .

Chunk.title: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV)
Chunk.text:
Mothership
The Mothership is the end of UHV progression, being required to reach Tier 9 planets and obtain Tengam, the magnetic material in UEV through UMV motors. Creating a Mothership requires launching a Shuttle Rocket while holding the necessary blocks and items, similar to a space station. The Shuttle Rocket's schematic is not found in a dungeon like previous schematics, but is instead crafted in the Assembly Line. Once the Mothership is built, engines must be placed on it and provided with fuel to travel to the Amun-Ra system, which contains the six Tier 9 planets; the only relevant to unlock UEV is Seth, which contains Tengam, as the Space Elevator is a better source of everything else on these planets. A small amount of dilithium from Neper is useful early in UEV. The Space Elevator can be used to travel to them, but only after obtaining MK-III motors, which require the DTPF. The Mothership also requires many previously optional steps in progression, such as the Nano Forge , Radox, and Kevlar.

- Interact with the rocket to enter it
- Interact again or sneak to leave it
- While on the rocket, press space to ignite the rocket and begin a launch; begins a 20-second countdown to launch, which cannot be cancelled.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
Chunk.text:
Rockets
Unlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station useful.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Launch Process
During the 20-second ignition period, the rocket produces 100 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 100\times Tier}} pollution/sec and will begin to shake and emit white smoke particles. After the launch begins, the launchpads will break, and the rocket will fly straight up without player steering. While the rocket is flying, it will produce 10000 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 10000\times Tier}} pollution/sec. Note that due to a bug the rocket will actually emit 20x that amount of pollution in version prior to 2.9. A GUI indicator on the left side of the screen will display the rocket's height relative to the world. If the rocket hits any blocks, it will stall and waste fuel, requiring player steering. If a rocket runs out of fuel while launching, it will explode.
Upon reaching maximum height (y~1100 for the overworld), the player will be transported away from their current dimension and be shown a catalog of solar systems and planets. Clicking on a planet allows the player to build a Space Station there or launch there as the destination on the upper right hand side. Clicking on the planet again will zoom in on it and display its moons and space stations, which can also be launched to. Blast Off \O/

Chunk.text:
Space Elevator
A Space Elevator.
The Space Elevator is a modular multiblock that can be made late in UV, after obtaining UHV circuits. Although it supports many different modules with various abilities, the only one obtainable in UV is the first tier of Space Mining Module, which can produce hundreds or thousands of ores per second using a non-consumed tiered mining drone, computation from a Quantum Computer , rods and drill tips of varying materials depending on the mining drone, and Helium, Bismuth, or Radon Plasma. It can also be configured to change the available ores and modify the chances of each ore being produced. Using the Space Elevator effectively requires robust ore processing, including any processing lines like the Platline or Naqline whose inputs come from ores, and sufficient automatic production of plasma and rods/drill tips of the relevant material. Although it is available in UV, it is expensive enough and available late enough in the tier that many players do not build it until UHV.
The Space Elevator can also be used to travel to any planet up to Tier 8, although it cannot be used to return, so it's necessary to bring a rocket or other means of teleportation to get back. This mechanic can be used to reach Tier 8 planets without the Tier 8 Rocket, and thereby gain earlier access to materials like Awakened Draconium and Infinity Catalyst. An upgrade to Tier 3 motors unlocks travel to Tier 9 planets in UIV.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Crafting Tier 2+ Rockets
Entrance to a Moon Dungeon
The NASA Workbench requires new schematics to craft higher tiers of rockets. These schematics are found in dungeons on planets in tier order. Tier 2 rocket schematics, for example, can be found in the reward room of Moon Dungeons. Dungeon entrances are deep holes on the surface that have unnatural brick blocks on the bottom.
The dungeons are naturally generated and so may be difficult to find. It is important to mark the location of each dungeon found as the coordinates are the same across each planet.
Higher tiers of rockets require different kinds of Rocket Fuels .

Chunk.title: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV)
Chunk.text: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV) is the ninth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. It unlocks Bioprocessors, infinity ingots, and Draconic Evolution. The overall goal is the construction of the Mothership and Shuttle rocket to reach the Amun-Ra system, which is required to get your foot through the door of UEV . In UHV, many previously optional processing chains and multiblocks become necessary for progression.

Chunk.title: Highly Ultimate Voltage (UHV)
Chunk.text:
Mothership
The Mothership is the end of UHV progression, being required to reach Tier 9 planets and obtain Tengam, the magnetic material in UEV through UMV motors. Creating a Mothership requires launching a Shuttle Rocket while holding the necessary blocks and items, similar to a space station. The Shuttle Rocket's schematic is not found in a dungeon like previous schematics, but is instead crafted in the Assembly Line. Once the Mothership is built, engines must be placed on it and provided with fuel to travel to the Amun-Ra system, which contains the six Tier 9 planets; the only relevant to unlock UEV is Seth, which contains Tengam, as the Space Elevator is a better source of everything else on these planets. A small amount of dilithium from Neper is useful early in UEV. The Space Elevator can be used to travel to them, but only after obtaining MK-III motors, which require the DTPF. The Mothership also requires many previously optional steps in progression, such as the Nano Forge , Radox, and Kevlar.

Chunk.title: Rockets
Chunk.text:
Launch Process
During the 20-second ignition period, the rocket produces 100 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 100\times Tier}} pollution/sec and will begin to shake and emit white smoke particles. After the launch begins, the launchpads will break, and the rocket will fly straight up without player steering. While the rocket is flying, it will produce 10000 × T i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 10000\times Tier}} pollution/sec. Note that due to a bug the rocket will actually emit 20x that amount of pollution in version prior to 2.9. A GUI indicator on the left side of the screen will display the rocket's height relative to the world. If the rocket hits any blocks, it will stall and waste fuel, requiring player steering. If a rocket runs out of fuel while launching, it will explode.
Upon reaching maximum height (y~1100 for the overworld), the player will be transported away from their current dimension and be shown a catalog of solar systems and planets. Clicking on a planet allows the player to build a Space Station there or launch there as the destination on the upper right hand side. Clicking on the planet again will zoom in on it and display its moons and space stations, which can also be launched to. The tier requirement of a launch is listed on the top of the screen; insufficient tier requirements prevent selecting a planet as a destination. The available destinations only depend on the tier of the rocket, not on the launch site.
Upon selecting a destination, the destination will be loaded in, and the player will descend riding some form of a Lunar Lander (Parachute, Lunar Lander, Landing Balloons, etc.). For the Moon , the player must press space to expend fuel and slow down the Lunar Lander to a descent rate slower than -20m/s to prevent an explosive crash landing. Upon landing, the player can exit the Lander by sneaking. The Lunar Lander will hold the rocket (with its fuel) and launchpads, used for a return flight. Punch to break it like a boat.
